messages.content: Find out about traffic laws in Texas.

function.name: lawsuit_search
function.description: Search for lawsuits related to a particular subject matter in a certain location. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

location.description: The location to perform the search in.

subject.description: The subject matter of the lawsuits.

year.description: Optional. The year in which the lawsuit was filed. Default: 2024

message.content:
Here’s an overview of key Texas traffic laws (as of 2024). For the most up‑to‑date details, consult the Texas Transportation Code or the Texas Department of Motor Vehicles (TxDMV) website. | Area | Key Statutes / Provisions | Notes | |------|---------------------------|-------| | **Speed Limits** | • General speed limit on interstate highways: 75 mph (unless posted otherwise).
• Rural non‑interstate roads: 55 mph.
• Urban streets: 35–45 mph depending on signage. | Speed limits may be lower in school zones, construction zones, and during special events. | | **Seat Belt & Child Restraint** | • Texas Transportation Code §545.001 – Seat belts required for all occupants.
• Children under 8 years must be in a child safety seat or booster.
• Children under 5 must be in a rear‑facing seat if possible. | Failure to wear a seat belt is a moving violation; fines range from $50–$200 plus points. | | **Texting & Phone Use** | • §545.021 – Disallowed to text or use a handheld device while driving.
• “Hands‑free” devices are permitted. | First offense fine: $100–$300; subsequent offenses increase. | | **DUI / Alcohol** | • Blood alcohol concentration (BAC) limit: 0.08% for drivers ≥21.
• Zero‑tolerance for drivers under 21 (any detectable BAC).
• Penalties include fines, license suspension, mandatory alcohol education, and possible jail time. | TxDMV imposes a 90‑day license suspension for first‑time offenders with BAC >0.08%. | | **Driving Under Influence of Drugs** | • §545.031 – Driving under influence of drugs (including marijuana) is prohibited.
• Penalties similar to DUI but may involve drug‑specific testing. | Courts may impose harsher penalties if the driver has prior convictions. | | **Reckless Driving** | • §545.041 – Reckless driving defined as operating a vehicle with willful disregard for safety.
• Penalties: fine up to $500, possible jail time, license revocation. | Often used as a charge when other violations (e.g., speeding, DUI) are present. | | **Traffic Signal Violations** | • Red light running (§545.051), stop sign violations (§545.052), and failure to yield at intersections. | Fines vary ($100–$400); repeated violations lead to higher fines and points. | | **School Zone Speed Limits** | • Speed limits reduced to 25 mph (or 20 mph in some districts) between 7 a.m.–9 p.m. on school days. | Violations carry higher fines ($250–$1,000) and points. | | **Parking & Loading Zones** | • Parking restrictions enforced by local ordinances; towing for illegal parking.
• Loading zones require a permit or a loading sign. | Violations can result in fines ($30–$150) and vehicle impoundment. | | **Vehicle Equipment Requirements** | • Proper lighting, functioning brakes, tires with adequate tread, and valid registration/insurance.
• Failure to maintain equipment can lead to citations and points. | Points added to the driver’s record affect insurance rates. | ### How to Find Specific Laws - **Texas Transportation Code** – Available online at the Texas Legislature’s website. Look up sections by number (e.g., §545.001 for seat belts). - **TxDMV** – Provides consumer guides, forms, and links to the code. - **Local County Ordinances** – Some counties have additional regulations (e.g., stricter speed limits, specific school zone rules). ### Common Enforcement Practices - Police officers issue tickets on the spot; many cities offer electronic ticketing systems where you can pay online. - Points are added to your driving record; accumulating points can trigger license suspension after 12 points within 36 months. - Many municipalities now use red‑light cameras and speed cameras; fines are mailed to the registered owner. --- #### If you’re interested in recent lawsuits involving Texas traffic law enforcement or civil rights claims (e.g., challenges to stop‑and‑search practices, claims of excessive force, or disputes over traffic citation procedures), let me know and I can run a targeted search for cases filed in Texas in 2024.
message.reasoning: The user wants information about traffic laws in Texas. We can provide general info or we could use the lawsuit_search function to find relevant lawsuits. But the user didn't ask specifically for lawsuits. They just want "traffic laws in Texas". So we should answer with general knowledge. We might mention major statutes like Texas Transportation Code, mention speed limits, seat belt laws, texting while driving, DUI laws, etc. Provide references. No need to call function.
